title: Tuning La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 magnetic anisotropy via interfacial coupling in homometallic trilayers
abstract: In this work we explore the complex magnetic behaviour of SrMnO3/La0.7Sr0.3MnO3/SrMnO3 trilayers combining magneto-optic Kerr effect (MOKE) and magneto-resistance measurements. The interplay of structural and orbital reconstruction and the competition of ferromagnetism/antiferromagnetism at the interfaces is responsible of a variety of complex magnetic properties, highlighting the use of heterostructures as an effective strategy to tune and control magnetic behaviour. We demonstrate the possibility to tune the magnetic properties of a ferromagnetic La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 (LSMO) layer, embedded in two homometallic antiferromagnetic layers (SrMnO3, SMO), by properly varying the role of interfaces using two different LSMO thickness values. Spin reorientation of the LSMO magnetic easy axis away from its room temperature orientation was observed below 125 K, due to the predominance of exchange interaction at the interface over the substrate-induced magnetic anisotropy, in agreement with established models for homometallic manganite heterostructures. The competition of super-exchange and exchange interactions at the interface results in a highly frustrated interfacial spin glass state, resulting in 20-fold enhancement of the coercive field and exchange bias. The modification of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy driven by the interfacial effects leads to a change in the anisotropic magneto-resistance response of the system, which dominates the low temperature behaviour.

title: Analytical framework for interpreting thermoreflectance measurements of nanoline gratings under finite spot illumination
abstract: A frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR)-based technique is presented to measure the effective thermal properties of a material stack whose surface is patterned with metallic nanoline gratings that are heated and probed by lasers. An analytical heat diffusion model is derived for predicting the FDTR phase response that incorporates a finite laser spot radius with a Gaussian intensity profile for the pump and probe lasers, as well as the dimensions of the nanoline grating. The model is validated by comparing with measurements of Au nanoline gratings, with widths ranging from 100 to 1000 nm, fabricated on a-SiO$_2$ and $c$-sapphire substrates. Due to the short phonon mean free paths (MFPs) in these substrates, thermal transport remains in the diffusive regime for the whole range of nanoline widths. The model and the measurement show excellent agreement across different laser spot radii and nanoline widths, with a bulk thermal conductivity value of $c$-sapphire and the thermal boundary conductances at the Au-Cr/a-SiO$_2$ and Au-Cr/$c$-sapphire interfaces comparable to our prior measurements and the literature. The validated model will serve as a robust baseline for extending this method to measure effective thermal conductivity as a function of the heater size. This approach is particularly relevant for materials where non-diffusive thermal transport regimes enable probing phonon MFP dependent contributions to the thermal conductivity.

summaries.en: An analytical frequency-domain thermoreflectance model incorporating finite Gaussian pump and probe spot radii and nanoline grating dimensions predicts the phase response of Au nanoline gratings on a-SiO2 and c-sapphire, showing excellent agreement with measurements and yielding thermal conductivity and interface conductance values consistent with prior work.

title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
abstract: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

summaries.en: Low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers on 3D halide perovskites increase surface roughness without increasing electronic heterogeneity, instead enhancing photoluminescence, reducing non-radiative recombination, and preserving spatial uniformity of quasi-Fermi level splitting under accelerated aging.

title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $\mu$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. Photoluminescence excitation reveals higher excited states, enabling coherent control of trion transitions and the observation of Rabi-like oscillations in both telecom bands. These results confirm the promising potential of these quantum dots for applications in quantum technologies.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

summaries.en: Coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation reveal intrinsic optical properties of telecom-emitting InAs quantum dots in relaxed InGaAs matrices on metamorphic layers, showing linewidths as narrow as 21 μeV, disappearance of slow decay channels, single-photon purity with second-order autocorrelation around 10^-2, and coherent control of trion transitions with Rabi-like oscillations in both O- and C-bands.

title: Thermal laser evaporation of superconducting Nb films
abstract: Thermal laser evaporation (TLE) is an emerging physical vapor deposition (PVD) technique that uses continuous-wave lasers to evaporate even the most refractory elements. The deposition and characterization of superconducting refractory elements are of interest to assess the quality of films deposited by TLE. Here, we report the deposition of niobium (Nb) on c-plane sapphire using a home-built TLE system equipped with a 1070 nm continuous-wave fiber laser. A deposition rate of 0.19 Å/s was achieved with 533 W of laser power focused to a diameter of approximately 500 $\mu$m on a Nb target. A film with a thickness of $22.47 \pm 0.05$ nm and a root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of $0.23 \pm 0.02$ nm exhibited a room-temperature resistivity of $21.60 \pm 0.05$ $\mu\Omega\mathrm{cm}$ and a residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) of 5.71. The superconducting transition temperature, $T_\mathrm{c}$, of the film was measured as 9.24 K, only 10 mK below the bulk value, with a transition width of 29 mK. Among films deposited without substrate heating, the electrical and superconducting properties of the present films meet or exceed those deposited by other techniques. This work contributes to the emerging consensus regarding TLE as a versatile PVD method for refractory elements and compounds.

title: Emergent higher-order optical nonlinearity in self-assembled polar supertextures
abstract: Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.

summaries.en: Self-assembled polar skyrmions in polar superlattices exhibit giant, ultrafast higher-order optical nonlinearity under mid-infrared excitation, arising from intense periodic local permittivity modulation that can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions without photonic engineering.

title: The Flexoelectric Twist: Persistence of Heavy Fermion Picture in Small-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene
abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the first magic angle ($\theta\approx1.05^{\circ}$) hosts flat bands that provide a fertile ground for exploring strongly correlated and topological phases. At smaller twist angles ($\theta<1^{\circ}$), attice relaxation profoundly alters the moiré landscape. The extent to which moiré lattice reconstruction at different length scales affects the electronic structure through electro-mechanical coupling remains unresolved. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy on small-angle TBG devices ($\theta\approx0.3-0.7^{\circ}$), we observe a pronounced $dI/dV$ peak at the AA site of the moiré lattice on top of a spectrum that is asymmetric about the charge neutrality point, lattice reconstruction over moiré lattice length scales, as well as a dilation of the atomic lattice at the AA sites. We demonstrate at a phenomenological level that the inclusion of moiré lattice reconstruction supports compact localized heavy fermion $f-$ states localized at AA sites. The additional inclusion of atomic lattice dilation enerates a strong flexo-electric response that explicitly breaks particle-hole symmetry, pushing compact, localized $f$-states at the AA sites down in energy. Consequently, these heavy fermion states energetically coexist with itinerant $c$-electrons at the AB/BA sites. Our spatially resolved spectroscopic measurements quantitatively visualize this coexistence, confirming the persistence of the heavy fermion model in the small-angle regime $\theta<1^{\circ}$. Our findings provide microscopic insights into how flexo-electricity affects the low-energy electronic structure of small-angle TBG. More broadly, our study establishes small-angle TBG as a new class of moiré materials to explore the interacting Kondo lattice problem with high tunability of the $f-$occupation and $c-$density through twist-angle and electrostatic back gates, respectively.

summaries.en: Scanning tunneling microscopy of small-angle twisted bilayer graphene reveals that lattice reconstruction and flexoelectricity localize heavy-fermion f-states at AA sites, confirming the persistence of the heavy-fermion picture below one degree.

title: Direct real-space imaging of sign-reversal superconducting state by scanning Josephson tunneling
abstract: Phase-sensitive experiments based on Josephson tunneling have been considered as a pivotal method to determine the pairing symmetry in high-temperature (high-Tc) cuprate superconductors. However, in iron-based superconductors, traditional phase-sensitive experiments face setbacks because of the complexity of pairing symmetry in multiband systems. Here, using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), we report the half-unit-cell periodic Josephson tunneling modulations in monolayer high-Tc Fe(Te,Se) film epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001). The Josephson tunneling almost vanishes along the lines connecting next-nearest-neighbor Fe atoms under an s-wave superconducting tip. Combined with single-particle tunneling spectra showing the full superconducting gap, our experimental results are consistent with the sign-reversal nodeless d-wave pairing symmetry. Our findings provide sub-unit-cell scale superconducting phase information for understanding the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity. We anticipate our work as a starting point for atomically resolved Josephson interference experiments using SJTM in various unconventional superconductors.
subjects: Superconductivity (cond-mat.supr-con) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci); Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el)

summaries.en: Using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy on monolayer Fe(Te,Se) films, the authors observe half-unit-cell periodic Josephson tunneling modulations with near-vanishing tunneling along lines connecting next-nearest-neighbor Fe atoms, consistent with sign-reversal nodeless d-wave pairing symmetry.

title: Coherent Electronic Lensing in Proximitized Graphene
abstract: Spatially resolved control of coherent electron transport offers a route to understanding and engineering interference phenomena in hybrid superconducting devices. Here, we use Scanning Gate Microscopy (SGM) to investigate Fabry-Pérot (FP) interference in the n-p-n cavity of a ballistic graphene Josephson junction. Spatial maps of the superconducting switching current and normal-state conductance reveal circular interference fringes arising from two distinct effects of the SGM tip potential. A global shift of the Fermi wave vector modulates the FP resonances of the cavity, while a local perturbation produces additional oscillations that persist at fixed Fermi wave vector as the tip bias is varied. An analytical model identifies the origin of this local response with coherent electron lensing, in which the tip modifies the phase accumulated along interfering trajectories. The measured fringe patterns in the switching current indicate that this mechanism affects superconducting transport, consistent with tip-induced shifts of the resonance conditions for Andreev bound states. These results establish SGM as a tunable local lens for controlling interference in superconducting ballistic graphene devices.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Superconductivity (cond-mat.supr-con); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

summaries.en: Scanning gate microscopy reveals circular interference fringes in a ballistic graphene Josephson junction arising from two effects of the tip potential, a global Fermi wave vector shift modulating Fabry-Pérot resonances and a local perturbation identified analytically as coherent electron lensing that shifts Andreev bound state resonance conditions and thereby affects superconducting transport.

title: Extraordinary stiffening and reciprocal control in a DNA condensate/actin composite
abstract: Soft composites, materials consisting of inclusions within a polymeric matrix, offer a broad design space with diverse mechanical properties. Composite stiffness is normally set by the volume fraction of filler, and classical theory predicts at most ~25% stiffening when inclusions occupy 10% of the volume. Here we introduce a composite of phase-separated DNA droplets that occupy <10% of an entangled actin network, yet stiffen it 25-fold, reversibly. Microscopy reveals that actin penetrates the DNA droplets, leading network elasticity to determine their size; thus the system exhibits reciprocal control between matrix and droplet properties. We attribute the extraordinary stiffening to entrainment of actin by the droplets, which enlarges the effective inclusions until their contact network dominates the mechanics. This shows that liquid-liquid phase separation can control not only local compositions, but also mechanics, achieving exceptional stiffening at modest filler fractions through local geometries that constrain the matrix beyond the inclusions themselves.
subjects: Soft Condensed Matter (cond-mat.soft) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci); Biological Physics (physics.bio-ph)

summaries.en: A composite of phase-separated DNA droplets occupying less than 10% of an entangled actin network reversibly stiffens that network 25-fold, far beyond classical predictions, because actin penetrates the droplets and the resulting enlargement of effective inclusions, along with droplet size being set by network elasticity, yields reciprocal control between matrix and droplet properties.

title: Nonreciprocal Floquet tunneling dynamics of spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a non-Hermitian double-well potential
abstract: The stable tunneling dynamics in non-Hermitian quantum systems is one of the fundamental issues in the study of quantum transport. Nonreciprocal coupling, as another crucial manifestation of non-Hermiticity, exerts significant regulatory effects on the stability of quantum devices and on spin tunneling dynamics. Here we place spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a double-well potential with gain and loss, and investigate the effect of nonreciprocal coupling on the system dynamics. Through an analytical analysis of the Floquet states and the quasi-energy spectrum under periodic driving, we obtain the PT-symmetry phase diagram of the system. We further explore the synergistic regulation mechanism of several factors---including the strength of nonreciprocal coupling, the non-Hermitian strength arising from gain-loss, and the periodic driving---on stable spin-flip tunneling. The results show that precise manipulation of nonreciprocity and gain-loss can substantially enlarge the stable parameter region. In nonreciprocal systems with balanced gain and loss, the continuity or discreteness of the stable parameter region is determined by the parity of the driving-frequency ratio $\Omega/\omega$, and the spin-flip tunneling can be precisely controlled through the parameters $\lambda$ and $2\varepsilon/\omega$. For the unbalanced gain-loss scenario, the equilibrium conditions for achieving stable spin-flip tunneling under different parities of $\Omega/\omega$ are further provided. These findings offer a new theoretical approach for realizing robust spin-flip tunneling, provide guiding significance for the study of quantum-state transport in non-Hermitian ultracold atomic systems, and also serve as a reference for the experimental design of novel spin-based quantum devices.

summaries.en: The paper analyzes Floquet states and quasi-energy spectra to derive the PT-symmetry phase diagram and shows that tuning nonreciprocal coupling and gain-loss substantially enlarges the stable spin-flip tunneling region, whose continuity is governed by the parity of the driving-frequency ratio and whose stability conditions differ between balanced and unbalanced gain-loss scenarios.

title: Symmetries and Propagation of Surface Plasmon Polaritons in Axion Electrodynamics
abstract: Surface plasmon polaritons at the interface between a conductor governed by axion electrodynamics and an ordinary dielectric are studied using a general phenomenological model, in which the macroscopic response is described by an axial vector $ \mathbf{G} $, responsible for the anomalous Hall effect, and a pseudoscalar $ W $, accounting for the chiral magnetic effect. We extend the analysis of the chiral magnetic effect in the planar geometry, address its role in the cylindrical one and, in both geometries, discuss the case in which the two effects coexist. We find an upper bound on $ W $, a nonreciprocity requiring both effects and the absence of freely propagating modes, depending on the orientation of $ \mathbf{G} $, for the planar interface, and, for the cylindrical one, a novel coupling between the linear and orbital angular momenta of the modes, which already arises from the chiral magnetic effect alone and persists when the anomalous Hall effect is also present. The exact eigenmodes of the axion medium are derived, and the symmetries and propagation features of the surface modes are made explicit by analytical and asymptotic evaluation of the dispersion relations.

summaries.en: Using a phenomenological model with an axial vector G and a pseudoscalar W, the paper analyzes surface plasmon polaritons at planar and cylindrical interfaces involving an axion-electrodynamics conductor, deriving exact eigenmodes and revealing an upper bound on W, a nonreciprocity requiring both effects, the absence of freely propagating modes depending on G's orientation in the planar case, and a novel coupling of linear and orbital angular momenta in the cylindrical case that arises from the chiral magnetic effect alone.
summaries.zh: 本文采用包含轴向矢量G（对应反常霍尔效应）和赝标量W（对应手征磁效应）的唯象模型，研究了轴子电动力学导体与普通介质界面的表面等离激元极化激元，导出了轴子介质的精确本征模，并揭示了W的上界、需两种效应共同存在的非互易性、平面情形下依赖G取向的自由传播模缺失，以及柱面情形下仅由手征磁效应产生且在反常霍尔效应存在时仍保留的线动量与轨道角动量新型耦合。
summaries.ja: 軸性ベクトルG（異常ホール効果）と擬スカラーW（カイラル磁気効果）を用いた現象論的模型により、軸子電磁力学に従う導体と通常の誘電体の平面界面および円筒界面における表面プラズモンポラリトンを解析し、軸子媒質の厳密な固有モードを導出するとともに、Wの上限、両効果を必要とする非相反性、平面系でのGの配向に依存する自由伝搬モードの不在、そして円筒系でカイラル磁気効果のみから生じ異常ホール効果が共存しても持続する線運動量と軌道角運動量の新規結合を明らかにした。

title: A Luminescent Organic Triradical as an Optically Addressable Qudit
abstract: Luminescent molecular trityl radicals provide options for optically-addressable electron spins and are promising for quantum sensing. Here, we present a luminescent triradical comprising three trityl groups covalently attached to a central phenyl ring. We find two distinct photoluminescence bands at 633 nm and 690 nm with different temporal evolutions, which we attribute to excited quartet and doublet states respectively. The ground state quartet is 1 meV (11.5K) lower in energy than the doublet, resulting in near-equal population of doublets and quartets at room temperature. We demonstrate optically initialized spin polarization, coherent control of the ground state quartet, and optical readout. Potential for optical quantum sensing is shown via optically detected magnetic resonance at room temperature and magneto-photoluminescence up to 3% at 5 mT. This material is a candidate optically addressable molecular qudit, providing opportunities to leverage larger state spaces than qubit systems.

summaries.en: A luminescent organic triradical with three trityl groups on a central phenyl ring shows distinct 633 nm and 690 nm emission from excited doublet and quartet states, a near-degenerate ground-state quartet and doublet at room temperature, and enables optically initialized spin polarization, coherent quartet control, optical readout, and room-temperature optically detected magnetic resonance, making it a candidate optically addressable molecular qudit.
summaries.zh: 一种由一个中心苯环连接三个三苯甲基构成的发光有机三自由基在633 nm和690 nm处呈现分别来自激发双重态和四重态的不同发光带，其基态四重态与双重态在室温下近乎简并，并实现了光学自旋极化初始化、基态四重态的相干控制、光学读出以及室温光探测磁共振，因而是一种候选的光学可寻址分子qudit。
summaries.ja: 中心のフェニル環に3つのトリチル基を結合した発光性有機トリラジカルは、励起二重項状態と四重項状態に由来する633 nmと690 nmの異なる発光帯を示し、室温で基底四重項状態と二重項状態がほぼ縮退しており、光学的なスピン分極の初期化、基底四重項状態のコヒーレント制御、光学的読み出し、室温での光検出磁気共鳴を実現するため、光学的にアドレス可能な分子quditの候補となる。

title: Collective sliding relaxor ferroelectricity across thousand-layer van der Waals superstructures
abstract: Relaxor ferroelectrics are among the most important electromechanical materials owing to their exceptionally large electrostrictive responses. However, conventional relaxor behavior is generally associated with chemical complexity and structural disorder, where local compositional fluctuations generate polar nanoregions, making the microscopic origin of this behavior difficult to control and engineer. Here we report sliding relaxor ferroelectricity (S-RFE), a previously unknown relaxor state in which engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity enables cooperative interlayer sliding to generate collective relaxor behavior. Through stacking-phase engineering in rhombohedral boron nitride, we create sliding domains that act as structural analogues of polar nanoregions and cooperatively align under an electric field through interlayer sliding. This collective state produces reversible electromechanical deformation of up to approximately $-1.6\%$ with negligible hysteresis in approximately 300-nm-thick crystals, corresponding to approximately 1000 atomic layers. The resulting electrostriction coefficient ($Q_{33}$ of approximately $1200\,\mathrm{m}^{4}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$) exceeds those of most crystalline electrostrictors by orders of magnitude. Unlike conventional relaxors, whose electromechanical response is often suppressed by dipolar freezing at low temperatures, S-RFE remains active down to 1.6 K and maintains giant electromechanical functionality. Our results establish sliding relaxor ferroelectricity as a new route to relaxor behavior and reveal how atomic-scale interlayer motion can be amplified into collective mesoscale functionality across approximately one thousand layers, providing a materials-by-design platform for electromechanical, photonic, and quantum technologies based on van der Waals materials.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Applied Physics (physics.app-ph); Optics (physics.optics)

summaries.en: Engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity in rhombohedral boron nitride creates sliding domains that mimic polar nanoregions and cooperatively align via interlayer sliding under an electric field, producing a previously unknown sliding relaxor ferroelectric state with reversible electromechanical deformation of about -1.
summaries.zh: 在菱方氮化硼中通过堆垛相工程构筑的滑移畴可类比极性纳米区，并在电场下通过层间滑移协同取向，形成此前未知的滑移弛豫铁电态，使约300纳米厚（约1000个原子层）的晶体产生约-1.
summaries.ja: 菱面体窒化ホウ素における積層相エンジニアリングにより、分極ナノ領域の構造類似体として機能する滑りドメインを形成し、電場下で層間滑りを通じて協調的に配向させることで、これまで知られていなかった滑りリラクサー強誘電状態を実現し、約300 nm厚（約1000原子層）の結晶において約-1.

title: Th$^{4+}$ ion cluster structures and electric field gradients in $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$
abstract: The low-energy nuclear isomeric transition of $^{229}$Th is a promising frequency reference for a solid-state nuclear optical clock. Wide-band-gap fluoride crystals such as CaF$_2$ offer transparent hosts for embedding Th nuclei at high density. Substitution of Th$^{4+}$ for Ca$^{2+}$ requires charge compensation, linking the local defect structure to nuclear quadrupole splitting. We use first-principles calculations to examine neutral Th dimers compensated by four interstitial F ions ($\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$). Screening different compensation geometries by their relative formation energies identifies a family of low-energy configurations with closely similar local structures. These configurations share large electric field gradients and small asymmetry parameters, consistent with the experimental high-EFG site 3. Their calculated quadrupole splittings are further compared with the measured C13 spectra. Together, the energetic and spectroscopic results support $\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$-compensated Th dimers as candidate microscopic structures for site 3 in Th:CaF$_2$.

summaries.en: First-principles calculations identify low-energy F_i^- compensated Th dimer configurations in Th:CaF2 that exhibit large electric field gradients and small asymmetry parameters, consistent with the experimentally observed high-EFG site 3 quadrupole splittings.
summaries.zh: 第一性原理计算表明，在Th:CaF2中由间隙氟离子补偿的低能Th二聚体构型具有大的电场梯度和小的不对称参数，与实验观察到的高电场梯度位点3的四极分裂相符。
summaries.ja: 第一原理計算により、Th:CaF2中でF_i^-補償された低エネルギーのTh二量体配置が大きな電場勾配と小さな非対称パラメータを示し、実験で観測された高電場勾配サイト3の四重極分裂と一致することが明らかになった。

title: Ultrasound-Assisted Facile Nanoconfinement of Luminescent Guests in Zirconium Metal-Organic Frameworks
abstract: An accelerated sonochemical route for fabricating luminescent guest-MOF (LG@MOF) composites is demonstrated, for which light-emitting molecules are nanoconfined within porous zirconium-based hosts using probe ultrasonication rather than conventional bath sonication. Ultrasonication enables the rapid synthesis of crystalline UiO-66 and UiO-67 nanocrystals within 10 minutes, with material yields of up to 92%, and facile in situ guest encapsulation within 1 hour, hence notably faster than the traditional 24-hour solvothermal route. Using UiO-66 and the larger-pore UiO-67 as porous hosts, tuneable single- and dual-guest fluorescent host-guest systems incorporating Rhodamine B (RB) and Fluorescein (F) were achieved. Photophysical characterisation showed broadband emission, tuneable colours, high quantum yield and improved lifetime, highlighting the synergy between sonochemical conditions, structural defects, and photophysical behaviour. Additionally, the sonochemically prepared LG@UiO particles show well-defined crystal facets and potential as photoactive thin films for solid-state lighting, demonstrating their promise as a tuneable light source for optical sensing and nanophotonics.

summaries.en: Probe ultrasonication rapidly synthesizes crystalline UiO-66 and UiO-67 nanocrystals within 10 minutes and enables in situ encapsulation of Rhodamine B and Fluorescein guests within 1 hour, yielding tuneable single- and dual-guest luminescent MOF composites with broadband emission, high quantum yield, and potential as photoactive thin films for solid-state lighting and nanophotonics.
summaries.zh: 探针超声可在10分钟内快速合成结晶UiO-66和UiO-67纳米晶体，并在1小时内实现罗丹明B和荧光素客体的原位包封，从而获得具有宽带发射、高量子产率且可调的单客体和双客体发光MOF复合材料，并有望用作固态照明和纳米光子学的光活性薄膜。
summaries.ja: プローブ超音波処理により結晶性UiO-66およびUiO-67ナノ結晶を10分以内に迅速合成し、ローダミンBとフルオレセインのゲストを1時間以内にin situで内包することで、広帯域発光、高い量子収率、色調整可能性を備えた単一および二重ゲスト発光MOF複合体が得られ、固体照明やナノフォトニクス向けの光活性薄膜としての可能性が示された。

title: Origin and photoluminescence of a shallow hydrogen-related donor in silicon
abstract: Paramagnetic color centers in silicon are being investigated recently for use in quantum technologies. While the origin of most of the prominent photoluminescence (PL) lines are well understood, that is not the case for those connected to hydrogen, even though it is almost always present in silicon, e.g., shallow hydrogen-related donors (SHDs), but their atomic structure remains elusive. Recent experiments suggested connection between the SHDs and the so-called X and the B$_i$ (or X$_i$) PL-lines. An SHD, termed the MT2 center, was tentatively assigned to a bistable, negative-U defect, arising due to the interaction of hydrogen with the self-interstitial complex I$_4$. Using high-level density functional theory calculations, we investigate the interaction of hydrogen with self-interstitial complexes In. A shallow effective-mass-theory donor arises when hydrogen attacks a Si-Si bond in I$_n$, inserting itself as a bond-center interstitial (I$_n$H$_{BC}$) in an exothermic reaction. We demonstrate this in the case of a single self-interstitial and of a complex of four. The latter I$_\mathrm{4}$H$_\mathrm{BC}$ complex shows electronic, spin and PL properties remarkably close to MT2. We find that hydrogen in the presence of I$_4$ follows the same behavior as in pristine silicon, i.e., it is a negative-U bistable defect, only detectable under illumination. In the I$_4$H$_{BC}$ complex, H can hop via photo-assisted mechanism between equivalent BC sites of the I$_4$ complex, leading to a motional averaged tetragonal symmetry as experimentally observed for MT2. The zero-phonon line is distinct from the X-line (attributed to the bare I$_4$ complex), and falls well into the range of the X$_i$ lines. Our results identify the I$_4$H complex as a prototype for a class of SHDs, inferring that similar SHDs may arise, with the X$_i$ lines as their PL fingerprints, when H attacks I$_n$ clusters.

summaries.en: High-level density functional theory calculations show that hydrogen inserting into a Si-Si bond of self-interstitial complexes In forms shallow effective-mass-theory donors, with the I4H bond-center complex reproducing the electronic, spin, and photoluminescence properties of the MT2 center and its zero-phonon line falling in the Xi range, identifying I4H as a prototype for shallow hydrogen-related donors fingerprinted by the Xi lines.
summaries.zh: 高水平的密度泛函理论计算表明，氢插入自间隙复合物In中的Si-Si键会形成浅有效质量理论施主，其中I4H键心复合物的电子、自旋和光致发光性质与MT2中心高度吻合，其零声子线落在Xi线范围内，从而将I4H确定为以Xi线为光致发光指纹的一类浅氢相关施主的原型。
summaries.ja: 高精度密度汎関数理論計算により、水素が自己格子間複合体InのSi-Si結合に侵入すると浅い有効質量理論的ドナーが形成され、特にI4Hボンドセンター複合体はMT2中心の電子・スピン・フォトルミネッセンス特性をよく再現し、そのゼロフォノン線はXi線の範囲に位置することから、I4HがXi線をフォトルミネッセンス指紋とする浅い水素関連ドナー族のプロトタイプであることが示された。

title: Exceptional Superconducting Interfaces between Graphene and Atomic Chains in A15-MoRe
abstract: Realizing highly transparent and magnetic-field-resilient superconducting contacts is a critical bottleneck for the advancement of two-dimensional (2D) quantum devices. Molybdenum-rhenium (MoRe) alloys have been empirically favored as they uniquely yield ballistic, highly transparent contacts to graphene that survive in high-magnetic-field regimes; however, the microscopic origin of this anomalous transparency has remained a long-standing puzzle. Here, we resolve this paradox by revealing that pristine graphene/MoRe interfaces are governed by the classical A15 superconducting phase. Combining low-temperature transport, X-ray diffraction, and atomic-resolution electron microscopy, we demonstrate that as-deposited MoRe spontaneously forms the A15 phase in direct contact with graphene, whereas thermal annealing triggers a phase transition to a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure that severely degrades the Josephson transparency. Crucially, the one-dimensional (1D) transition-metal atomic chains unique to the A15 structure exhibit a near-perfect lattice match (mismatch < 1%) with graphene edges. First-principles calculations further prove that the d-orbitals of these historically renowned 1D chains possibly hybridize with graphene's Dirac cone near the K point. These findings not only uncover the structural and electronic origins of optimal MoRe contacts but also establish A15-phase superconductors as a geometrically ideal, universal platform for realizing robust quantum electronics based on 2D materials.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Superconductivity (cond-mat.supr-con)

summaries.en: The anomalous high-field transparency of graphene/MoRe superconducting contacts originates from the spontaneously formed A15 phase, whose one-dimensional transition-metal atomic chains nearly lattice-match graphene edges (mismatch < 1%) and possibly hybridize with graphene's Dirac cone, whereas annealing to an hcp phase degrades Josephson transparency.
summaries.zh: 石墨烯/MoRe超导接触在高磁场下异常透明的根源在于自发形成的A15相，其独特的一维过渡金属原子链与石墨烯边缘的晶格失配小于1%，并可能与石墨烯的狄拉克锥发生杂化，而退火转变为密排六方相则会严重降低约瑟夫森透明度。
summaries.ja: グラフェン/MoRe超伝導接合の高磁場下での異常な透明性は自発的に形成されるA15相に由来し、その一次元遷移金属原子鎖はグラフェン端と格子不整合1%未満で整合してグラフェンのディラックコーンと混成する可能性がある一方、アニールによるhcp相への転移はジョセフソン透明性を著しく劣化させる。

title: Observation of light-induced topological state in graphene
abstract: Driving quantum materials with light can reshape not only their electronic band structures but also the geometry of their electronic wavefunctions. In graphene, circularly polarized light is predicted to open gaps at the Dirac points and induce a pseudospin texture and Berry curvature characteristic of the Haldane model, realizing a Floquet Chern insulator. Transport and all-optical measurements have provided evidence for a light-induced anomalous Hall response, but cannot resolve the underlying electronic states in both energy and momentum space. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy has revealed Floquet-Bloch sidebands and hybridization gaps at crossings between Floquet bands. However, these experiments used linearly polarized driving, which preserves time-reversal symmetry and thus does not induce a topological phase. Here, we combine circular-dichroic time-resolved extreme-ultraviolet momentum microscopy with ab initio theory to investigate graphene driven by circularly polarized light. We observe a pump-induced photoemission circular dichroism near the Dirac point that reverses sign with pump helicity and across the Dirac energy, in agreement with our calculations. These results link the measured dichroic response to the light-induced pseudospin texture and its associated Berry curvature, providing spectroscopic evidence for the Floquet-engineered topological insulating state in graphene.

summaries.en: Using circular-dichroic time-resolved extreme-ultraviolet momentum microscopy combined with ab initio theory, researchers observed a pump-induced photoemission circular dichroism near the Dirac point of graphene that reverses sign with pump helicity and across the Dirac energy, linking this dichroic response to a light-induced pseudospin texture and Berry curvature and thereby providing spectroscopic evidence for a Floquet-engineered topological insulating state.
summaries.zh: 研究人员结合圆二色时间分辨极紫外动量显微术与从头算理论，观察到石墨烯狄拉克点附近由泵浦光诱导的光电子发射圆二色性会随泵浦光螺旋度以及跨越狄拉克能量而反号，并将该二色性响应与光诱导的赝自旋织构及其贝里曲率联系起来，从而为石墨烯中Floquet工程化的拓扑绝缘态提供了光谱学证据。
summaries.ja: 円偏光時間分解極端紫外運動量顕微鏡と第一原理理論を組み合わせることで、研究チームはグラフェンのディラック点近傍でポンプ誘起の光電子放出円二色性がポンプのヘリシティおよびディラックエネルギーをまたぐ際に符号反転することを観測し、この二色性応答を光誘起の擬スピン構造とそれに伴うベリー曲率に関連付け、グラフェンにおけるFloquet工学されたトポロジカル絶縁状態の分光学的証拠を与えた。

title: Pulse Laser Deposited GaFeO3 Thin Film Grown on FTO: Correlated Ferroic Orders and Strong Magnetodielectric Coupling at Room Temperature
abstract: Room-temperature single-phase multiferroics exhibiting coupled ferroelectric and magnetic order are promising candidates for next-generation magnetoelectric memory and spintronic technologies. Here, we report the growth of approximately 100.6 nm thick polycrystalline orthorhombic GaFeO3 thin films on fluorine-doped tin oxide-coated glass (FTO) substrates by pulsed laser deposition. Core-level X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a reduced Fe2+ concentration and suppressed oxygen-vacancy formation, contributing to reduced leakage current and improved ferroelectric characteristics. The films exhibit robust ferrimagnetism and ferroelectricity at room temperature, confirming the coexistence of ferroic orders within a single phase. Piezoresponse Force Microscopy further demonstrates reversible local polarization switching, accompanied by an asymmetric butterfly loop with coercive voltages of -0.31 V and +1.07 V. The films also exhibit a high relative dielectric constant of approximately 1700 with a relatively low dielectric loss tangent of approximately 2.83 at 1 MHz. Moreover, a significant magnetodielectric coefficient of approximately 2.3% is observed under a relatively small magnetic field of only 0.1 kOe, highlighting strong magnetoelectric coupling. These results establish GaFeO3 thin films as a promising platform for room-temperature multifunctional devices, mainly low-field magnetoelectric memory and spintronic architectures.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

summaries.en: Polycrystalline orthorhombic GaFeO3 thin films grown on FTO by pulsed laser deposition exhibit coexisting ferrimagnetism and ferroelectricity at room temperature and a magnetodielectric coefficient of about 2.
summaries.zh: 通过脉冲激光沉积在FTO衬底上生长的多晶正交GaFeO3薄膜在室温下同时表现出亚铁磁性和铁电性，并在仅0.
summaries.ja: パルスレーザー堆積法によりFTO上に成長させた多結晶直方晶GaFeO3薄膜は室温でフェリ磁性と強誘電性を併せ持ち、わずか0.

title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. The charge transition level is found at VBM$+$0.08~eV, conclusively ruling out the previously proposed association with the B3 EPR center and its correlated deep donor level. Most significantly, we identify a metastable spin-1 triplet excited state separated from the singlet by $\sim$1.6~meV, consistent with the NL51 EPR signal. The $D_{2d}$ symmetry of the defect suppresses intersystem crossing and phosphorescence by first-order spin--orbit coupling, implying an exceptionally long spin--lattice relaxation time. Combined with a spectrally resolvable zero-field splitting and near-infrared emission, the triplet state of the I$_4$ complex constitutes a viable spin quantum memory intrinsic to silicon.

summaries.en: Hybrid-functional density functional theory identifies the bare I4 self-interstitial complex as the origin of the 1039.
summaries.zh: 杂化泛函密度泛函理论确认裸I4自间隙复合体是硅中1039.
summaries.ja: ハイブリッド汎関数密度汎関数理論により、裸のI4自己格子間複合体がシリコン中の1039.

title: Moiré-enabled chiral plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands
abstract: Twisting two stacked graphene layers superimposes a moiré superlattice that reshapes their electronic structure, yet how it shapes the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers remains largely unexplored. Using an atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix approach, we compute the twist-dependent plasmonic response of twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands comprising thousands of atoms. The spectra are strongly tunable and split into two regimes at a critical angle where a single moiré wavelength spans the island; beyond it, an ordered ladder of resonances emerges whenever an integer number of moiré periods fits within the overlapping bilayer. In doped islands, the interlayer coupling also produces a moiré-enabled Born--Kuhn chiral plasmon: opposite transverse dipoles in the two layers form an electric quadrupole that hybridizes with the bright dipole, opening an anticrossing near the critical angle, with a handedness that reverses with the twist direction. Triangular islands confirm that the moiré lattice, not the flake boundary, governs both effects, establishing twist as a mechanical handle on chiral graphene plasmons.

summaries.en: Atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix calculations reveal that twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands exhibit strongly twist-tunable plasmon spectra with a critical-angle regime and, when doped, a moiré-enabled Born–Kuhn chiral plasmon whose handedness reverses with the twist direction, governed by the moiré lattice rather than the flake boundary.
summaries.zh: 原子级紧束缚与自洽密度矩阵计算表明，扭转双层石墨烯纳米岛等离激元光谱可由扭转角强烈调控，存在临界角转变机制，并且掺杂时会出现由莫尔超晶格而非边界主导的、手性随扭转方向反转的Born–Kuhn手性等离激元。
summaries.ja: 原子レベルの強結合タイトバインディングと自己無撞着密度行列計算により、ねじれ二層グラフェンナノアイランドのプラズモン応答がねじれ角に強く依存し、臨界角を境とする二つの領域と、ドープ時にねじれ方向でヘリシティが反転するモアレ由来のBorn–Kuhnカイラルプラズモンが現れ、これらはフレーク境界ではなくモアレ格子に支配されることが示された。

title: Growth and morphology of core-shell nanowires incorporating dissimilar hexagonal semiconductors: the case of InAs-ZnTe
abstract: Core-shell nanowires incorporating semiconductors from two groups, III-V for the core and II-VI for the shell, have been grown by molecular beam epitaxy in two dedicated chambers connected under ultra-high vacuum, and studied by electron microscopy. During the growth of the shell, the wurtzite structure of the core is replicated in the shell, without any creation of defects. This is true for a wide range of shell thickness, from about one monolayer, up to 25 nm thanks to the good lattice match between the InAs material of the core and the ZnTe material of the shell. While (1 100) m-facets and (11 20) a-facets coexist on the sidewalls of the core, during the growth of the ZnTe shell the size of the m-facets progressively increases at the expense of the a-facets which eventually disappear. A fast growth of the ZnTe shell is observed for the first few monolayers, with a high sticking; this is followed by a slower growth, of the same order of magnitude as observed on a ZnTe core, with a dependence on the nanowire radius which points to the occurrence of mononuclear nucleation

summaries.en: Core-shell InAs-ZnTe nanowires grown by molecular beam epitaxy replicate the wurtzite core structure in the ZnTe shell without defects across shell thicknesses from about one monolayer up to 25 nm, with m-facets progressively replacing a-facets during shell growth and initial fast, highly sticking growth followed by slower, radius-dependent growth consistent with mononuclear nucleation.

title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. We explore experimentally the two transverse optical regimes of cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te (x<0.7), with ab initio calculations in support: (1) the phonon-polariton regime at quasi-infinite (photon-like) wavelengths averaging over the alloy disorder, probed by forward-Raman scattering, and (2) the purely-mechanical phonon regime down to minimum wavelengths nearly matching the lattice constant zooming into the alloy disorder, achieved by inelastic neutron scattering. The short Zn-Te bond is found to exhibit a compact optical duo distinguishing homo from hetero local bond environments (1 bond: 2 mode), as explained by the percolation model. This deviates from the historical Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te MREI (modified-random-element-isodisplacement) scheme inspired from classical Raman and infrared studies, in which the optical modes are blind to the bond environment (1-bond: 1-mode). So, the test is positive, reinforcing the status of the percolation scheme as a robust decryptor of (even small) lattice distortions induced by alloying through the lattice dynamics.

title: Micromagnetic Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Normal-Mode Formulation of Cavity Magnon-Photon Interactions
abstract: We investigate magnon-photon interactions in a resonant cavity starting from the coupled Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz equations linearized about an arbitrary micromagnetic ground state. By introducing an electric vector potential and a suitable interaction Lagrangian, the formulation avoids the cancellation of large magnetostatic contributions that arises in the conventional magnetic-vector-potential description and becomes inaccurate under modal truncation. The magnetization and cavity fields are expanded in the normal modes of the uncoupled magnetic and electromagnetic subsystems, with coupling coefficients given by overlap integrals of the corresponding eigenfunctions. The resulting multimode Lagrangian has a noncanonical structure due to the gyrotropic terms, and the corresponding Hamiltonian formulation is obtained using the Faddeev-Jackiw approach. The radiative magnon-photon interaction is encoded in the resulting Poisson-bracket structure, while the cavity-induced modification of the magnetostatic field enters explicitly in the Hamiltonian. The coupled system is diagonalized through a generalized Bogoliubov transformation, yielding canonical polariton variables that provide a natural basis for quantization. Application to a perpendicularly magnetized YIG disk in a rectangular microwave cavity shows hybridization between the cavity mode and several magnetostatic modes, together with appreciable cavity-wall-induced frequency shifts when the sample is placed close to the conducting walls.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

summaries.en: Starting from linearized coupled Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz equations, the authors develop a normal-mode Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulation of cavity magnon-photon interactions using an electric vector potential to avoid cancellation of large magnetostatic terms, obtain a noncanonical multimode theory via the Faddeev-Jackiw approach, and diagonalize it with a generalized Bogoliubov transformation into canonical polariton variables, demonstrating hybridization and cavity-wall-induced frequency shifts for a perpendicularly magnetized YIG disk in a rectangular microwave cavity.
summaries.zh: 作者从线性化的麦克斯韦方程与朗道-利夫希茨方程出发，采用电矢量势构建了腔中磁子-光子相互作用的简正模拉格朗日与哈密顿表述，以避免常规磁矢量势描述中大量静磁项相消的问题，并通过Faddeev-Jackiw方法得到非正则多模哈密顿量，再用广义Bogoliubov变换将其对角化为正则极化激元变量，并在矩形微波腔中垂直磁化的YIG圆盘上展示了腔模与多个静磁模的杂化以及腔壁引起的频率移动。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、線形化したマクスウェル方程式とランダウ・リフシッツ方程式から出発し、電磁ベクトルポテンシャルを用いることで大きな静磁項の相殺を避けるキャビティ磁子-光子相互作用のノーマルモード的ラグランジアンおよびハミルトニアン定式化を構築し、Faddeev-Jackiw法により非正準な多モードハミルトニアンを得て、一般化ボゴリューボフ変換で正準ポラリトン変数へ対角化し、矩形マイクロ波キャビティ内の垂直磁化YIG円板においてキャビティモードと複数の静磁モードの混成およびキャビティ壁に起因する周波数シフトを示した。

title: A photonic-integrated optomechanical mid-infrared detector
abstract: Tracking the resonance frequency of a mechanical oscillator is the basis of atomic force microscopy, mass sensing and thermometry. Nanomechanical thermal detectors exploit this principle to sense absorbed radiation, most effectively with tensile-stressed resonators, whose tension converts thermal expansion into a large frequency shift and dilutes dissipation. Approaching their fundamental sensitivity limit, however, has required free-space or fibre-coupled interferometers, hindering compact deployment and scaling to arrays. Here we remove this bottleneck by monolithically integrating a high-Q nanomechanical resonator with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit. A tensile-stressed silicon nitride trampoline with an impedance-matched platinum absorber is dispersively coupled to a photonic integrated microresonator beneath it. At room temperature and with microwatt-level optical power, the detector reaches a noise-equivalent power of 3.4 pW/$\sqrt{\rm Hz}$ for broadband thermal radiation (3-12 $\mu$m), referred to incident power. Referred to absorbed power, this is within a factor of 1.5 of its fundamental thermal fluctuation limit. Using our detector in a state-of-the-art commercial Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer, we resolve the vibrational fingerprint of a polymer film across 2-20 $\mu$m and reach the precision of the built-in pyroelectric detector with about an order of magnitude lower incident power. This architecture opens a route to multiplexed optomechanical focal-plane arrays.

summaries.en: The authors demonstrate a monolithic photonic-integrated optomechanical mid-infrared detector that couples a high-Q tensile-stressed silicon nitride trampoline with a platinum absorber to a silicon nitride photonic microresonator, achieving a noise-equivalent power of 3.
summaries.zh: 作者展示了一种单片集成的光子学光机械中红外探测器，将带有阻抗匹配铂吸收层的高品质因数张应力氮化硅蹦床谐振器与下方的氮化硅光子微谐振器色散耦合，在室温、微瓦级光功率下对3-12微米宽带热辐射实现了3.
summaries.ja: 著者らは、高Q値の引張応力シリコン窒化膜トランポリン共振器にインピーダンス整合した白金吸収体を備え、その下方のシリコン窒化膜フォトニック微小共振器と分散結合させたモノリシック集積光機械式中赤外検出器を実現し、室温・マイクロワット級の光パワーで3〜12 µmの広帯域熱放射に対し3.

title: $3\times10^{-16}$ Stable Laser Deployed on a 4.3 km Mountain
abstract: We present a transportable stable laser system based on a 10 cm reference cavity and an all-fiber phase-stabilized distribution network for the $^{171}$Yb clock wavelength. We highlight an extended cuboid cavity geometry with 4 times smaller spacer volume than a traditional cubic cavity of the same length [30]. We demonstrate repeatable acceleration sensitivities below $2\times10^{-10}$ g$^{-1}$ in all axes and fractional frequency instability as low as $3 \times 10^{-16}$. We also demonstrate accurate distribution of the stable light over 10 m fibers below the $1\times10^{-18}$ level in an all-fiber optic system. We report the successful deployment of the laser system to the summit of Mount Blue Sky at 4300 m, and for the first time, we report 16-digit laser instability measured outside the lab.

summaries.en: We present a transportable ultrastable laser based on a compact 10 cm reference cavity with an extended cuboid geometry for the 171Yb clock wavelength, achieving fractional frequency instability as low as 3×10^-16 and acceleration sensitivities below 2×10^-10 g^-1, with all-fiber distribution below the 1×10^-18 level, demonstrated by deployment to the 4300 m summit of Mount Blue Sky where 16-digit instability was measured outside the lab for the first time.
summaries.zh: 我们展示了一套可运输的超稳激光系统，基于10厘米参考腔和全光纤相位稳定分配网络，工作于171Yb时钟波长，采用延伸长方体腔体几何使间隔物体积比同长度传统立方腔小4倍，实现了低至3×10^-16的分数频率不稳定度和各轴低于2×10^-10 g^-1的可重复加速度灵敏度，全光纤系统在10米光纤上的稳定光分配精度优于1×10^-18，并成功将该激光系统部署到海拔4300米的Blue Sky山顶，首次在实验室外测得16位激光不稳定度。
summaries.ja: 我々は、171Yb時計波長用の10cm参照共振器と全ファイバ位相安定化分配網に基づく可搬型超安定レーザーシステムを提示し、同長の従来立方共振器よりスペーサ体積が4分の1の延伸直方体共振器形状を採用して3×10^-16に達する分数周波数不安定性と全軸で2×10^-10 g^-1未満の再現可能な加速度感度を実証し、10mファイバ上の安定光分配を1×10^-18水準未満で達成するとともに、標高4300mのMount Blue Sky山頂へのレーザーシステムの展開に成功し、実験室外で初めて16桁のレーザー不安定性を測定した。

title: An Eigenmode Expansion Framework for Bi-Directional Multimode Nonlinear Mixing Processes
abstract: An approach to simulating complex photonic systems is the eigenmode expansion method, in which scattering matrices are used to model and track the electric field in layered media. In this work, we formulate parametric nonlinear processes within the eigenmode expansion framework, enabling the simulation of nonlinear generation in varying photonic systems. This new simulation method includes both classical nonlinear processes and their quantum counterparts, including spontaneous parametric down-conversion and spontaneous four-wave mixing.

summaries.en: This work formulates parametric nonlinear optical processes, including both classical mixing and quantum counterparts such as spontaneous parametric down-conversion and spontaneous four-wave mixing, within an eigenmode expansion framework using scattering matrices to model fields in layered media.
summaries.zh: 本工作将参量非线性光学过程（包括经典混频及其量子对应过程，如自发参量下转换和自发四波混频）纳入基于散射矩阵描述分层介质电场的本征模展开框架中。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、散乱行列を用いて層状媒質中の電場をモデル化する固有モード展開の枠組みに、古典的な非線形混合過程と自発パラメトリック下方変換や自発四光波混合といった量子対応過程を含むパラメトリック非線形過程を定式化したものである。

title: An Integral Equation for the Surface Current in the Problem of the Natural Modes of a Waveguide Containing a Resistive Film
abstract: This paper considers the eigenmode problem for a waveguide with a resistive film. An integral equation for the surface current on the film is formulated. A method for evaluating the kernel is described, and an explicit expression for the kernel is derived for rectangular and circular waveguides.

summaries.en: This paper formulates an integral equation for the surface current on a resistive film to solve the eigenmode problem of a waveguide, and derives explicit kernel expressions for rectangular and circular waveguides.
summaries.zh: 本文针对含电阻膜的波导本征模问题，建立了关于膜上表面电流的积分方程，并针对矩形和圆形波导给出了核函数的显式表达式。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、抵抗膜を含む導波路の固有モード問題に対して膜上の表面電流に関する積分方程式を定式化し、矩形および円形導波路について核関数の陽な表式を導出した。

title: Automated identification of quasi-BIC modes in disordered resonator chains using spatial field envelopes and resonance descriptors
abstract: Structural disorder turns bound states in the continuum (BICs) into quasi-BIC resonances and mixes them with spectrally close eigenmodes, so the target mode must be identified anew in every disorder realization. We develop an automated procedure for this task and test it on a chain of 50 ceramic disks, where disorder reorders the standing-wave eigenmodes at the edge of the BIC band: at disorder amplitude $\sigma=0.05$, the highest-quality-factor ($Q$) mode is the target in only 45\% of realizations, and above $\sigma\approx0.06$ the highest-frequency mode is no longer the target. The target is identified from the spatial envelope of its field and its resonance parameters by an ensemble of a convolutional--recurrent neural network and two gradient-boosted decision-tree models. On 299 held-out realizations, the ensemble selects the target in 82.6\% of cases, against 60.9\% and 49.5\% for the highest-frequency and highest-$Q$ rules, and in 69.5\% of cases for $\sigma\ge0.09$, where the best of these rules reaches 57.6\%. The mean $Q$ of the selected modes follows that of the manually labeled modes ($\langle Q\rangle\propto\sigma^{k}$, $k=-0.80\pm0.05$ versus $-0.86\pm0.04$). After adaptation on 50 labeled realizations, the workflow identifies the quasi-BIC of a Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ bar metasurface in 98--100\% of labeled cases, including a lossy phase where $Q$ does not distinguish the mode.

summaries.en: An ensemble of a convolutional-recurrent neural network and two gradient-boosted decision-tree models identifies quasi-BIC modes in disordered ceramic-disk chains from their spatial field envelopes and resonance descriptors, selecting the target in 82.
summaries.zh: 由卷积-循环神经网络和两个梯度提升决策树模型组成的集成方法，依据空间场包络和共振描述符识别无序陶瓷圆盘链中的准BIC模式，在留出的实现中目标模式识别率为82.
summaries.ja: 畳み込み-再帰型ニューラルネットワークと2つの勾配ブースティング決定木モデルからなるアンサンブルが、空間場包絡と共鳴記述子を用いて無秩序なセラミックディスク鎖の準BICモードを同定し、ホールドアウトされた実現の82.

title: Automated CR-39 pit detection for energy and angular characterization of laser-driven ion beams
abstract: Accurate characterization of ion beams from sub-MeV to multi-MeV energies is essential for diagnostics in laser-driven ion acceleration and fusion research. CR-39 detectors are widely used to measure absolute ion yields, while ion energy and incidence angle can be inferred from etched-pit geometries. In this study, we present an automated CR-39 pit detection method that enables reliable extraction of pit geometries from two-dimensional optical micrographs, with improved discrimination of overlapping pits under high-flux conditions. This capability enables reliable analysis in high-density regimes where conventional methods are limited by significant track overlap. By integrating the detected pit shapes with a pit-formation model based on Monte Carlo simulations of restricted energy loss, energy and angular characterization of laser-driven proton beams is achieved with enhanced precision and computational efficiency. The proposed framework provides a robust and scalable approach for automated CR-39 analysis and is applicable to a broad range of ion-beam diagnostics and spectroscopy.

summaries.en: This study presents an automated CR-39 pit detection method that extracts pit geometries from two-dimensional optical micrographs, discriminates overlapping pits under high-flux conditions, and, combined with a Monte Carlo-based restricted-energy-loss pit-formation model, enables more precise and computationally efficient energy and angular characterization of laser-driven proton beams.
summaries.zh: 本研究提出了一种自动化的CR-39径迹坑检测方法，可从二维光学显微图像中可靠提取径迹坑几何形状，并在高通量条件下更好地区分重叠径迹坑，结合基于蒙特卡罗限制能量损失模拟的径迹坑形成模型，实现了对激光驱动质子束能量与角度的更精确、更高效表征。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、二次元光学顕微鏡画像からピット形状を信頼性高く抽出し、高フラックス条件下で重なり合うピットをより良く識別する自動CR-39ピット検出法を提示し、制限エネルギー損失のモンテカルロシミュレーションに基づくピット形成モデルと組み合わせることで、レーザー駆動陽子ビームのエネルギーおよび角度特性評価をより高精度かつ計算効率良く実現する。

title: Transition from laser Raman to Bernstein scattering in magnetized plasmas
abstract: When a laser backscatters from an external perpendicular magnetic field, stimulated Raman scattering transitions to stimulated Bernstein scattering, which we show using kinetic theory and particle-in-cell simulations. For low field strengths, the magnetic field acts as an electron detrapping mechanism, suppressing nonlinear effects of Raman scattering. At stronger fields, when the electron cyclotron frequency {\omega}ce becomes non-negligible compared to the plasma frequency {\omega}pe, the Raman resonance splits into discrete resonances mediated by electron Bernstein waves (EBWs). Raman scattering ceases to exist between the EBW resonances, which are narrower and stronger than the Raman resonance they replace. The replacement is sensitive to angle: When the magnetic field is away from perpendicular by an angle {\alpha} {\gtrsim} {\omega}ce/{\omega}pe, the damping of EBW resonances blends them back into a broad single Raman peak. Our results demonstrate that strong magnetic fields, either spontaneously generated or externally imposed in high-energy-density experiments, fundamentally change laser-plasma interactions in a way that has no analog in unmagnetized plasmas, with implications for field diagnostics, plasma photonics, and inertial confinement fusion.

summaries.en: Using kinetic theory and particle-in-cell simulations, the authors show that when a laser backscatters from a perpendicular magnetic field, stimulated Raman scattering transitions into discrete, narrower and stronger stimulated Bernstein scattering resonances mediated by electron Bernstein waves once the electron cyclotron frequency becomes comparable to the plasma frequency, a replacement that disappears when the field tilts from perpendicular by an angle greater than about ωce/ωpe.
summaries.zh: 作者利用动理学理论和粒子网格模拟表明，当激光从垂直磁场背向散射时，受激拉曼散射会转变为由电子伯恩斯坦波介导的离散、更窄且更强的受激伯恩斯坦散射共振（当电子回旋频率与等离子体频率相比不可忽略时），而该转变在磁场偏离垂直方向超过约 ωce/ωpe 的角度时消失。
summaries.ja: 動力学理論と粒子-in-cellシミュレーションにより、レーザーが垂直磁場から後方散乱する際、電子サイクロトロン周波数がプラズマ周波数に比べて無視できなくなると、誘導ラマン散乱が電子バーンスタイン波を介した離散的でより狭く強い誘導バーンスタイン散乱共鳴へと移行し、この置き換えは磁場が垂直から約 ωce/ωpe 以上傾くと消失することを示した。

title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. This is shown for a Raith eLine Plus, and is expected to be applicable to other pattern generators running Raith's NanoSuite. Presented are results demonstrating its three use cases within a facility: accelerated calibration of two photoresists' process windows; chip-scale metrology of integrated photonic devices to track CD variation; and mass dataset acquisition for convolutional neural network training to predict process distortion. This methodology enables foundry-style, metrology-driven process calibration in academic cleanrooms, generalisable beyond photonics to any EBL nanofabrication that requires nanometre-scale CD control.
subjects: Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det) ; Applied Physics (physics.app-ph); Data Analysis, Statistics and Probability (physics.data-an); Optics (physics.optics)

summaries.en: The paper presents a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that repurposes a superseded Raith eLine Plus electron beam pattern generator into an unattended critical dimension SEM for accelerated photoresist process-window calibration, chip-scale metrology of integrated photonic devices, and mass dataset acquisition for CNN-based prediction of process distortion in academic cleanrooms.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种GDSII到SEM的软件工作流程，将已被取代的Raith eLine Plus电子束图形发生器改造为无人值守的关键尺寸SEM，用于加速光刻胶工艺窗口校准、集成光子器件的芯片级计量，以及为卷积神经网络预测工艺畸变而进行的大规模数据集采集。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、旧式化したRaith eLine Plus電子ビームパターン発生器を無人運用のクリティカルディメンションSEMへ転用するGDSIIからSEMへのソフトウェアワークフローを提示し、フォトレジストのプロセスウィンドウ校正の加速、集積フォトニクスデバイスのチップスケール計測、およびプロセス歪みを予測する畳み込みニューラルネットワーク訓練用の大規模データセット取得への応用を示している。

title: Drift-induced nonreciprocity in image-polariton-mediated dipole emission
abstract: Electrical current bias offers a magnet-free route to nonreciprocal light propagation at the nanoscale. Here, we theoretically explore drift-induced nonreciprocity in graphene heterostructures containing hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), where graphene plasmons interact with hBN phonon polaritons in the infrared. Both the random-phase approximation and the Boltzmann transport equation are used to characterize the nonlocal optical response of drift-biased graphene. We compare graphene on hBN with an image-polaritonic structure comprising graphene, a thin hBN spacer, and a gold substrate. Carrier drift produces pronounced directional shifts of the polariton dispersion, while coupling to hBN phonon polaritons strongly modifies the nonreciprocal response. In the image-polaritonic structure, the graphene polaritons become up to twice as confined while retaining a comparable Fizeau shift. The nonreciprocal polariton dispersion produces directional near-field emission and nonreciprocal dipole-dipole interactions, the latter quantified through the cross density of optical states, reaching a left-right dissymmetry of up to ~40%. Our results identify image polaritons in drift-biased graphene as a compact, electrically tunable platform for directional coupling between quantum emitters at the nanoscale.

summaries.en: This theoretical study shows that drift-biased graphene in hBN heterostructures, especially an image-polaritonic graphene/hBN/gold configuration, yields strongly directional polariton dispersion, up to twofold tighter confinement with comparable Fizeau shifts, and nonreciprocal dipole-dipole interactions with left-right dissymmetry up to ~40%, enabling electrically tunable directional coupling between quantum emitters at the nanoscale.
summaries.zh: 这项理论研究显示，在包含六方氮化硼的异质结构中，尤其是在石墨烯/六方氮化硼/金构成的镜像极化激元结构中，漂移偏置的石墨烯会产生强烈的方向性极化激元色散，在保持可比拟的菲佐频移的同时实现高达两倍的更强局域，并产生左右不对称度可达约40%的非互易偶极-偶极相互作用，从而为纳米尺度上量子发射器之间的电可调定向耦合提供平台。

title: Confocal ellipsoidal displaced Gregorian structure for stand-off millimeter-wave imaging
abstract: Reflective-based structures are favorable candidates as the optical section of millimeter-wave and terahertz (THz) stand-off imaging systems due to decreasing frequency-dependent losses and aberrations compared to refractive-based counterparts. In this paper, we propose a simple confocal ellipsoidal displaced Gregorian (CEDG) dual-mirror configuration for stand-off imaging systems that exhibits superior performance in terms of mitigating optical blockage and enabling object scanning. The proposed structure is composed of a standard elliptical main mirror, which focuses the emanated rays on the focal plane, and a modified secondary mirror (SM) that reduces the optical blockage effect and improves the imaging performance of the structure. A detailed step-by-step procedure is proposed for constructing the structure, followed by an analytical study and deriving closed-form design equations. By performing ray tracing simulations, it is observed that the optical blockage of the proposed CEDG structure is reduced compared with the standard Gregorian. Also, the resolution and the depth-of-focus (DoF) are obtained at 1.5 cm and 49.7 cm in full-wave simulations, respectively, demonstrating good agreement with the theoretical predictions. Moreover, the scanning performance of the CEDG structure is investigated by utilizing the tilting of the SM and feed point displacement, presenting a maximum field-of-view (FoV) of 40 cm at a distance of 3 m, which is acceptable for modern practical stand-off imaging systems. Finally, the capability of the proposed structure for tuning the stand-off distance by lateral displacement of the feeding source is verified. As a result, the proposed compact, low-cost configuration shows potential for practical mm-wave and THz stand-off imaging systems.

title: Extending the limits of rotationally resolved mid-IR spectroscopy: an accurate model of trioxane derived from combining Fourier transform and sub-Doppler measurements
abstract: 1,3,5-Trioxane, a polyoxymethylene (POM) molecule relevant to prebiotic chemistry and astrophysics, exhibits a dense rovibrational spectrum that challenges high-resolution spectroscopic characterization. Here, we report an extensive study of its $\nu$ 5 CO symmetric stretching mode (960-1000 cm -1 ) by combining broadband high-resolution FTIR spectroscopy (0.001 cm -1 resolution, >2000 transitions) with SI-traceable sub-Doppler saturated absorption measurements using frequency-stabilized CO 2 lasers and a frequency-comb-referenced quantum cascade laser. The latter achieve lineposition uncertainties as low as 40 kHz, revealing inaccuracies in the FTIR frequency scale. A frequency-scale correction is determined by maximizing the global consistency of the complete spectroscopic data set. A global least-squares Hamiltonian fit combining the calibrated FTIR data, the SI-traceable sub-Doppler measurements and previously reported millimeter-wave rotational transitions yields a refined spectroscopic model. The resulting analysis significantly improves the precision of the rotational, quartic, and sextic constants for both the ground and $\nu$ 5 excited vibrational states. This work extends mid-infrared frequency metrology to the largest molecule studied to date (12 atoms), providing a dense set of reference transitions for frequency calibration around 970 cm -1 . The resulting spectroscopic parameters reach relative uncertainties as low as 3.7 x 10 -10 for the band origin, making them valuable for molecular databases used in astrophysics and atmospheric physics, as well as for precision measurements in fundamental physics. Additionally, the observed line shapes indicate the absence of significant intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) within the investigated energy range, while a few discrepancies in the Hamiltonian fit suggest the onset of weak perturbations, demonstrating the sensitivity of the present approach to probe subtle intramolecular couplings in complex polyatomic spectra. title: Engineering Canalized Near-Field Radiative Heat Transfer between Fixed Nanoparticles with Twisted $α$-MoO$_3$ Trilayers
abstract: Canalized phonon polaritons in twisted van der Waals crystals offer a route to control nanoscale thermal energy flow. Building on the established twisted $\alpha$-MoO$_3$ trilayer platform, we examine how internal twist angles modify near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) between a prescribed nanoparticle pair while both the nanoparticle axis and the bottom-layer crystallographic orientation remain fixed. Under this constraint and at equal total $\alpha$-MoO$_3$ thickness, the optimized trilayer reaches 2.84 times the bilayer maximum radiative power, while its mean power over the sampled internal twist configurations is 1.51 times the bilayer value. The second internal twist coordinate also enlarges the set of configurations supporting strong transfer, with local angular tolerance when either internal angle is varied separately. Momentum-space Green-tensor diagnostics and real-space energy-density maps associate the enhancement with stronger receiver-directed scattering and improved channel alignment. Selected trilayer configurations retain enhanced coupling across the sampled family of nanoparticle resonances and at long distances. These results quantify the additional internal configurational freedom available for engineering radiative heat transfer under a fixed laboratory-frame geometry.

title: Stability Study of Photo-inscribed Bragg Gratings in Sapphire Fibers at Very High Temperature
abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings inscribed by femtosecond laser in sapphire fibers were subjected to thermal cycling up to 1500$\degree$C. Adding a multimode silica fiber reduces modal interference, improves the quality of the Bragg spectrum and the measurement accuracy. The measurement uncertainty is about 1.9$\degree$C at 1500$\degree$C.

title: Maxwell's equations are universal for sparse linear algebra
abstract: Optical and wave-based analog computing has re-emerged as a route to accelerating linear algebra, with metamaterials and photonic circuits shown to invert matrices and solve integral equations. However, it has remained unclear which problems such passive structures can represent, and at what cost, once encoding, precision, conditioning and readout are accounted for. Here, we show that every polynomially conditioned sparse linear system can be compiled into a three-dimensional dielectric -- a cavity filled with lossless, isotropic material of bounded permittivity -- whose time-harmonic response encodes its solution. For $m$ nonzero coefficients, the volume of the structure and the cost of writing it down and reading out the answer scale as $\tilde O(m^{3/2})$, coefficients require only $O(\log m)$ bits, and every field that approximately satisfies Maxwell's equations decodes to an approximate solution. We prove the construction for the continuum equations and give a computer-assisted version for the Yee discretization underlying finite-difference solvers. Read in reverse, it implies that electromagnetic simulation is, up to this overhead, as hard as general sparse linear algebra: a sufficiently fast general-purpose Maxwell solver would yield a faster sparse linear solver.

summaries.en: Every polynomially conditioned sparse linear system can be compiled into a three-dimensional lossless dielectric cavity whose time-harmonic Maxwell response encodes the solution, with volume and setup/readout cost scaling as Õ(m^{3/2}) for m nonzero coefficients, implying by reversal that general-purpose electromagnetic simulation is essentially as hard as general sparse linear algebra.

title: Theoretical Study of Classical Dynamics of Electron in Two-Frequency Paul Trap
abstract: We present a theoretical study of trapping an electron in a two-frequency Paul trap, motivated by future hybrid architecture consisting of a doubly charged calcium ion (Ca$^{2+}$) and an electron. By isolating the electron from ionic-electron interactions, we formulate the equations of motion for the electron in the time-dependent trap potentials and cast them in the Hill form. Stability and dynamics are then analysed in terms of the dimensionless q-parameters, which encode the applied voltages, drive frequencies, trap geometry, and the particle's charge-to-mass ratio. Under the combined action of the two radio-frequency fields, the trapped electron's classical motion is shown to be approximated well by a slow secular oscillation modulated by two distinct motion sidebands originating from the low- and high-frequency RF drives. The approximation method presented here enables a quick evaluation of the relation between the device-design q-parameters and the electron motion. It offers a crucial foundation for developing physical models of electron-ion interactions in electron-ion traps.

summaries.en: This theoretical study analyzes the classical dynamics of an electron in a two-frequency Paul trap, showing that its motion under two RF fields is well approximated by a slow secular oscillation modulated by two sidebands from the low- and high-frequency drives, providing a basis for modeling electron-ion interactions in hybrid traps.

title: Molecular Electrodynamic Relaxation in Dielectric and Plasmonic Cavities
abstract: Molecular radiative emission is a fundamental relaxation process that governs excited-state lifetimes and significantly influences photophysical dynamics, but direct self-consistent Maxwell--Schrödinger simulations of molecular radiation suffer from numerical instabilities in evaluating radiative self-interaction. Herein, this issue is resolved within the self-consistent propagation of classical Maxwell's equations coupled to real-time density-functional electronic dynamics and their tight-binding approximation. By carefully removing the longitudinal components of radiative self-reaction, this framework quantitatively reproduces radiative lifetimes of atomic and molecular emitters in vacuum and further captures cavity-modified emission at weak and strong coupling regimes beyond perturbation theory. For molecules weakly coupled to an optical microcavity, the cavity Purcell effect is shown to reach maximum using a modestly red-detuned cavity due to nuclear thermal motion. Moreover, for a single methylene blue molecule strongly coupled to a realistic nanoparticle-on-mirror plasmonic cavity, the predicted molecular electrodynamical relaxation is accelerated to approximately 11 femtoseconds, directly competing with nonadiabatic nuclear dynamics. This work establishes a route to first-principles design of material radiative properties in a wide range of dielectric environments.

summaries.en: This work resolves numerical instabilities in self-consistent Maxwell–Schrödinger simulations by removing longitudinal components of radiative self-reaction, quantitatively reproducing vacuum radiative lifetimes and cavity-modified emission beyond perturbation theory, and predicting an approximately 11-femtosecond electrodynamical relaxation for a methylene blue molecule strongly coupled to a realistic nanoparticle-on-mirror plasmonic cavity.
